	stars = "rbxassetid://118405531972534",
}

-- Each look: material, optional texture, reflectance, how far the color is pulled toward white
-- (whiten) or a fixed color, a see-through range (minTransparency / maxTransparency), and its
-- animation: rainbow (hue cycles), pulse (glows brighter and back), shimmer (a light sheen washes
-- over it), fade (breathes in and out). Tuned so each reads clearly through the outline.
Chams.LOOKS = {
	-- Smooth, slightly glossy color: the all-rounder.
	Aura = { material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, reflectance = 0.18, whiten = 0.05 },
	-- Bright glowing body.
	Neon = { material = Enum.Material.Neon, minTransparency = 0.12, pulse = 0.18, pulseSpeed = 2.4 },
	-- Plain matte color.
	Flat = { material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic },
	-- Mirror metal in a pale tint of the color, with a sheen.
	Chrome = { material = Enum.Material.Foil, reflectance = 0.6, whiten = 0.45, shimmer = 0.25 },
	-- Rippling metal: water pattern on the body and a strong moving sheen.
	["Liquid Metal"] = { material = Enum.Material.Foil, texture = Chams.TEXTURES.water, reflectance = 0.8, whiten = 0.25, shimmer = 0.4, scroll = Vector2.new(0.35, 0.6), tile = 4 },
	-- Polished gold.
	Gold = { material = Enum.Material.Foil, fixed = Color3.fromRGB(255, 190, 55), reflectance = 0.45, shimmer = 0.3 },
	-- Clear, sparkling crystal.
	Diamond = { material = Enum.Material.Glass, whiten = 0.65, reflectance = 0.5, minTransparency = 0.3, shimmer = 0.35 },
	-- Tinted glass.
	Glass = { material = Enum.Material.Glass, reflectance = 0.2, minTransparency = 0.4, whiten = 0.15 },
	-- Frosted ice.
	Ice = { material = Enum.Material.Ice, fixed = Color3.fromRGB(170, 225, 255), reflectance = 0.2, minTransparency = 0.2 },
	-- Glossy black stone with a colored sheen.
	Obsidian = { material = Enum.Material.Glass, fixed = Color3.fromRGB(18, 16, 26), reflectance = 0.55, shimmer = 0.15 },
	-- Molten glow, slowly throbbing.
	Lava = { material = Enum.Material.Neon, texture = Chams.TEXTURES.water, fixed = Color3.fromRGB(255, 95, 20), pulse = 0.35, pulseSpeed = 1.6, scroll = Vector2.new(0.1, -0.35), tile = 4 },
	-- Electric glow that throbs fast.
	Plasma = { material = Enum.Material.Neon, pulse = 0.35, pulseSpeed = 4, minTransparency = 0.1 },
	-- Radioactive green.
	Toxic = { material = Enum.Material.Neon, fixed = Color3.fromRGB(110, 255, 60), pulse = 0.3, pulseSpeed = 3 },
	-- Shimmering energy shield (the material animates by itself).
	Ropes = { material = Enum.Material.ForceField },
	-- Energy shield cycling through the rainbow.
	Rainbow = { material = Enum.Material.ForceField, rainbow = true },
	-- Aurora pattern in your chams color, with a moving sheen (the Rainbow look cycles colors).
	Holographic = { material = Enum.Material.ForceField, texture = Chams.TEXTURES.aurora, shimmer = 0.3, scroll = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.2) },
	-- Starfield.
	Galaxy = { material = Enum.Material.ForceField, texture = Chams.TEXTURES.stars, scroll = Vector2.new(0.12, 0.06), shimmer = 0.15 },
	-- Green code rain.
	Matrix = { material = Enum.Material.ForceField, texture = Chams.TEXTURES.matrix, fixed = Color3.fromRGB(60, 255, 90), scroll = Vector2.new(0, -1.2) },
	-- Soft pearl white.
	Pearl = { material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, reflectance = 0.3, whiten = 0.6, shimmer = 0.15 },
	-- Shiny plastic.
	Glossy = { material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, reflectance = 0.45 },
	-- Breathes in and out of view.
	Fade = { material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, fade = true },
	-- Glowing edges only.
	Wireframe = { material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, wireframe = true },
	-- Rippling blue water: glassy body, flowing ripples and a sheen.
	Water = { material = Enum.Material.Glass, texture = Chams.TEXTURES.water, fixed = Color3.fromRGB(40, 150, 255), reflectance = 0.35, minTransparency = 0.25, shimmer = 0.3, scroll = Vector2.new(0.15, -0.4), tile = 5 },
	-- Dark smoked glass with your color only in its glowing rim and sheen.
	Void = { material = Enum.Material.Glass, fixed = Color3.fromRGB(22, 10, 40), reflectance = 0.4, minTransparency = 0.12, shimmer = 0.2 },
	-- Northern lights: the aurora pattern cycling through every color.
	Aurora = { material = Enum.Material.ForceField, texture = Chams.TEXTURES.aurora, rainbow = true },
	-- Crackling energy: bright neon that flickers fast.
	Electric = { material = Enum.Material.Neon, pulse = 0.6, pulseSpeed = 14, minTransparency = 0.15 },
	-- Sci-fi hologram: rippling see-through light with a sheen rolling over it.
	Hologram = { material = Enum.Material.ForceField, texture = Chams.TEXTURES.water, whiten = 0.2, shimmer = 0.35 },
	-- Used by the ghost trail copies (not listed in the menu).
	Ghost = { material = Enum.Material.ForceField },
}
Chams.LOOK_NAMES = {
	"Aura", "Neon", "Flat", "Chrome", "Liquid Metal", "Gold", "Diamond", "Glass", "Ice", "Obsidian",
	"Lava", "Plasma", "Toxic", "Ropes", "Rainbow", "Holographic", "Galaxy", "Matrix", "Pearl", "Glossy",
	"Fade", "Wireframe", "Water", "Void", "Aurora", "Electric", "Hologram",
}
-- The material dropdowns: "None" at the top turns that material off.
Chams.LOOK_CHOICES = { "None" }
for _, name in ipairs(Chams.LOOK_NAMES) do
	table.insert(Chams.LOOK_CHOICES, name)
end

-- R6 limb name to the BodyPart a package (CharacterMesh) replaces.
Chams.BODY_PARTS = {
	Head = Enum.BodyPart.Head,
	Torso = Enum.BodyPart.Torso,
	["Left Arm"] = Enum.BodyPart.LeftArm,
	["Right Arm"] = Enum.BodyPart.RightArm,
	["Left Leg"] = Enum.BodyPart.LeftLeg,
	["Right Leg"] = Enum.BodyPart.RightLeg,
}

-- How much bigger the shell is than the part it wraps.
Chams.INFLATE = 1.05
Chams.PACKAGE_INFLATE = 1.1

-- Every chams model and the Chams object that owns it. A sweep below removes any model whose
-- owner stopped updating it (player left, feature turned off mid-way), so nothing is left frozen.
Chams.owners = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

task.spawn(function()
	while isCurrentRun() do
		task.wait(1)
		local now = os.clock()
		for proxy, owner in pairs(Chams.owners) do
			local stale = not owner.lastUpdate or now - owner.lastUpdate > 2
			if not proxy.Parent or (stale and not owner.frozen) then
				Chams.owners[proxy] = nil
				if proxy.Parent then
					pcall(owner.clear, owner)
				end
			end
		end
	end
end)

function Chams.new(parent)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Chams)
	self.highlight = Instance.new("Highlight")
	self.highlight.Name = "AquaChamsHL"
	self.highlight.Enabled = false
	self.highlight.DepthMode = Enum.HighlightDepthMode.AlwaysOnTop
	self.highlight.Parent = parent
	self.proxy = nil
	-- Source part -> its shell.
	self.parts = {}
	-- Shell -> the Texture objects on its faces (textured looks on plain parts).
	self.faceTextures = {}
	self.model = nil
	self.scannedAt = 0
	self.lookName = nil
	self.appliedKey = nil
	return self
end

---The package mesh replacing an R6 limb, if the character wears one.
local function packageMesh(source, character)
	local bodyPart = Chams.BODY_PARTS[source.Name]
	if not (bodyPart and character and source.Parent == character) then
		return nil
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(character:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("CharacterMesh") and child.BodyPart == bodyPart and child.MeshId ~= 0 then
			return child
		end
	end
	return nil
end

---A shell with the same shape as `source`, a little bigger, in the look's material.
local function makeShell(source, character, look)
	local shell
	local textured = false
	-- A textured mesh whose pattern is tinted to the cham color (returned third).
	local tintMesh = nil

	if source:IsA("MeshPart") then
		-- MeshId can't be set from a script, so the mesh part itself is copied.
		local archivable = source.Archivable
		source.Archivable = true
		local ok, copy = pcall(source.Clone, source)
		source.Archivable = archivable
		if not (ok and copy) then
			return nil
		end
		copy:ClearAllChildren()
		shell = copy
		shell.Size = source.Size * Chams.INFLATE
		-- No texture on mesh shells: a mesh texture replaces the part's color, so hats, hair,
		-- heads and mesh bodies came out as white glass instead of the cham color. ForceField is the
		-- exception: it draws the texture as a moving pattern tinted in the part's color.
		local forceField = look.material == Enum.Material.ForceField
		shell.TextureID = forceField and look.texture or ""
		textured = true
	else
		shell = Instance.new("Part")
		shell.Size = source.Size
		local package = packageMesh(source, character)
		local mesh = source:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")
		if package then
			local packageShell = Instance.new("SpecialMesh")
			packageShell.MeshType = Enum.MeshType.FileMesh
			packageShell.MeshId = "rbxassetid://" .. tostring(package.MeshId)
			-- The pattern goes on the mesh, tinted to the cham color with VertexColor (an untinted
			-- mesh texture replaces the color and came out white).
			packageShell.TextureId = look.texture or ""
			tintMesh = look.texture and packageShell or nil
			-- Package limbs get a little more room: at 1.05 their real mesh poked through in places.
			packageShell.Scale = Vector3.one * Chams.PACKAGE_INFLATE
			packageShell.Parent = shell
			textured = true
		elseif mesh then
			local meshShell = Instance.new("SpecialMesh")
			meshShell.MeshType = mesh.MeshType
			meshShell.MeshId = mesh.MeshId
			meshShell.Offset = mesh.Offset
			meshShell.Scale = mesh.Scale * Chams.INFLATE
			local fileMesh = mesh.MeshType == Enum.MeshType.FileMesh
			meshShell.TextureId = fileMesh and look.texture or ""
			tintMesh = (fileMesh and look.texture) and meshShell or nil
			meshShell.Parent = shell
			textured = fileMesh
		else
			shell.Size = source.Size + Vector3.one * 0.1
		end
	end

	shell.Name = ""
	shell.Anchored = true
	shell.CanCollide = false
	shell.CanQuery = false
	shell.CanTouch = false
	shell.CastShadow = false
	shell.Massless = true
	shell.Transparency = 0
	shell.LocalTransparencyModifier = 0
	shell.Material = look.material
	shell.Reflectance = look.reflectance or 0
	shell.CFrame = source.CFrame

	-- Plain blocks and head meshes can't take a mesh texture; put the image on each face instead.
	-- Not for ForceField looks (Holographic, Galaxy, Matrix): stamped on as flat tiles it made the
	-- body look blocky, while the ForceField shimmer on its own glows like the head does.
	local faces = nil
	if look.texture and not textured and look.material ~= Enum.Material.ForceField then
		faces = {}
		for _, face in ipairs(Enum.NormalId:GetEnumItems()) do
			local texture = Instance.new("Texture")
			texture.Face = face
			texture.Texture = look.texture
			-- Bigger tiles on busy patterns (water, lava), which looked like static at 2 studs.
			texture.StudsPerTileU = look.tile or 2
			texture.StudsPerTileV = look.tile or 2
			texture.Parent = shell
			table.insert(faces, texture)
		end
	end

	-- One table instead of three return values: the obfuscated build mixed up multiple returns
	-- (faces came back as a boolean, so every chams update errored and the ESP went with it).
	return { shell = shell, faces = faces, tint = tintMesh }
end

---Show the real body again (after "hide body under chams").
function Chams:restoreSources()
	if not self.hidden then
		return
	end
	self.hidden = false
	-- The preview copy was hidden by its own Transparency.
	if self.viewHidden then
		for source, transparency in pairs(self.viewHidden) do
			if source.Parent then
				source.Transparency = transparency
			end
		end
		self.viewHidden = nil
		return
	end
	for source in pairs(self.parts) do
		if source.Parent and source.LocalTransparencyModifier ~= 0 then
			source.LocalTransparencyModifier = 0
		end
	end
end

---The glow layer: a bigger copy of a shell in ForceField, which draws as a bright shimmering rim
---around the body's edges (a soft Neon haze in the ESP preview, where ForceField doesn't draw).
local function makeGlow(shell, source, inViewport)
	local glow = shell:Clone()
	for _, child in ipairs(glow:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Texture") or child:IsA("WeldConstraint") or child:IsA("SelectionBox") then
			child:Destroy()
		end
	end
	local mesh = glow:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")
	if glow:IsA("MeshPart") then
		glow.Size = source.Size * 1.16
	elseif mesh and mesh.MeshType == Enum.MeshType.FileMesh then
		mesh.Scale = mesh.Scale * 1.12
	elseif mesh then
		mesh.Scale = mesh.Scale * 1.12
		glow.Size = shell.Size * 1.12
	else
		glow.Size = source.Size + Vector3.one * 0.34
	end
	glow.Material = inViewport and Enum.Material.Neon or Enum.Material.ForceField
	if glow:IsA("MeshPart") then
		glow.TextureID = ""
	end
	glow.Reflectance = 0
	glow.CastShadow = false
	return glow
end

---Remove every shell (the look changed, or the chams are going away).
---What a part looks like shape-wise (size, mesh, package): when this changes, its shell is remade.
function Chams.shapeKey(part, character)
	local mesh = part:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")
	local package = packageMesh(part, character)
	return part.ClassName .. tostring(part.Size)
		.. (part:IsA("MeshPart") and part.MeshId or "")
		.. (mesh and (mesh.MeshId .. tostring(mesh.MeshType) .. tostring(mesh.Scale)) or "")
		.. (package and tostring(package.MeshId) or "")
end

---Stop listening to the old model (see Chams:watch).
function Chams:unwatch()
	for _, connection in ipairs(self.watchers or {}) do
		connection:Disconnect()
	end
	self.watchers = {}
end

---Remove a part's shell (and glow) the instant the part leaves the model. Shells are welded to
---their part, so when a gun was put away (Quick Swap) its shells lost the weld and fell to the
---floor until the next rescan; now they go with it.
function Chams:watch(model)
	self:unwatch()
	table.insert(self.watchers, model.DescendantRemoving:Connect(function(part)
		local shell = self.parts[part]
		if shell then
			self.parts[part] = nil
			self.faceTextures[shell] = nil
			shell:Destroy()
		end
		local glow = self.glows and self.glows[part]
		if glow then
			self.glows[part] = nil
			glow:Destroy()
		end
	end))
	-- New parts (a gun you just pulled out) get shells on the very next update instead of waiting
	-- for the half-second rescan.
	-- Also meshes and packages (CharacterMesh) arriving after a respawn, so blocky shells get
	-- their real shape right away.
	table.insert(self.watchers, model.DescendantAdded:Connect(function(object)
		if object:IsA("BasePart") or object:IsA("DataModelMesh") or object:IsA("CharacterMesh") then
			self.scannedAt = 0
		end
	end))
	-- The model itself leaving the world (a held tool going back to the backpack): all shells go.
	if not self.viewport then
		table.insert(self.watchers, model.AncestryChanged:Connect(function()
			if not model:IsDescendantOf(workspace) then
				self:clear()
			end
		end))
	end
end

function Chams:clearShells()
	self:unwatch()
	self:restoreSources()
	for _, glow in pairs(self.glows or {}) do
		glow:Destroy()
	end
	self.glows = {}
	for _, shell in pairs(self.parts) do
		shell:Destroy()
	end
	table.clear(self.parts)
	table.clear(self.faceTextures)
	self.shapeKeys = {}
	self.tints = {}
	self.appliedKey = nil
end

---Keep one shell per visible part of `model`, and move every shell onto its part.
Chams.sync = LPH_NO_VIRTUALIZE(function(self, model, now, look)
	if not (self.proxy and self.proxy.Parent) then
		self.proxy = Instance.new("Model")
		self.proxy.Name = "AquaChams"
		self.parts, self.faceTextures = {}, {}
		self.scannedAt = 0
		-- The proxy has to be in the world (not the camera) for welds to carry the shells.
		-- In a preview viewport (the ESP preview) it lives in the viewport instead.
		self.proxy.Parent = self.viewport or workspace
		Chams.owners[self.proxy] = self
	end
	self.lastUpdate = now

	-- Parts come and go (hats, tools, respawns), so rescan twice a second.
	if model ~= self.model or now - self.scannedAt > 0.5 then
		if model ~= self.model then
			self:clearShells()
			self.model = model
			self:watch(model)
		end
		-- A little random spread so every player's rescan doesn't land on the same frame (a hitch
		-- twice a second in full servers).
		self.scannedAt = now + math.random() * 0.15

		local seen = {}
		self.shapeKeys = self.shapeKeys or {}
		for _, part in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
			-- Held tools get no shells: switching guns broke the tool's grip a moment before it left
			-- the hand, and its shell dropped to the floor. (Tool chams, where the tool is the model,
			-- still get them.)
			local heldTool = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Tool")
			if heldTool and heldTool ~= model then
				continue
			end
			-- A preview part hidden under its chams still counts by its real transparency.
			local hiddenAs = self.viewHidden and self.viewHidden[part]
			if part:IsA("BasePart") and part.Name ~= "HumanoidRootPart" and (hiddenAs or part.Transparency) < 0.99 then
				seen[part] = true
				-- A part whose shape changed since its shell was made gets a new shell. Right after a
				-- respawn the body is still plain blocks; the game adds the package meshes a moment
				-- later, and the shells used to stay blocky.
				local key = Chams.shapeKey(part, model)
				local oldShell = self.parts[part]
				if oldShell and self.shapeKeys[part] ~= key then
					self.parts[part] = nil
					self.faceTextures[oldShell] = nil
					oldShell:Destroy()
					local oldGlow = self.glows and self.glows[part]
					if oldGlow then
						self.glows[part] = nil
						oldGlow:Destroy()
					end
					self.appliedKey = nil
				end
				if not self.parts[part] then
					self.shapeKeys[part] = key
					local made = makeShell(part, model, look)
					local shell = type(made) == "table" and made.shell or nil
					local faces = shell and type(made.faces) == "table" and made.faces or nil
					local tintMesh = shell and typeof(made.tint) == "Instance" and made.tint or nil
					if shell then
						self.tints = self.tints or {}
						self.tints[shell] = tintMesh
						-- Welded to its part, so the engine carries it: no Lua work per frame
						-- (moving every shell every frame cost a lot of FPS in big servers).
						shell.CFrame = part.CFrame
						shell.Parent = self.proxy
						-- Viewports have no physics, so preview shells stay anchored and are moved below.
						if not self.viewport then
							local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
							weld.Part0 = part
							weld.Part1 = shell
							weld.Parent = shell
							shell.Anchored = false
						end
						-- The preview window can't draw ForceField, Neon or Glass (they came out as
						-- flat plastic), so those are drawn glossy there instead.
						if self.viewport and (shell.Material == Enum.Material.ForceField or shell.Material == Enum.Material.Neon
							or shell.Material == Enum.Material.Glass) then
							shell.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
							shell.Reflectance = math.max(shell.Reflectance, 0.25)
							-- A ForceField pattern on plastic would cover the color with the raw image.
							if shell:IsA("MeshPart") then
								shell.TextureID = ""
							end
						end
						self.parts[part] = shell
						self.faceTextures[shell] = faces
						self.appliedKey = nil

						-- Glow layer around it.
						if self.glowEnabled and not look.wireframe then
							self.glows = self.glows or {}
							local glow = makeGlow(shell, part, self.viewport ~= nil)
							glow.CFrame = part.CFrame
							glow.Anchored = true
							glow.Parent = self.proxy
							if not self.viewport then
								local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
								weld.Part0 = part
								weld.Part1 = glow
								weld.Parent = glow
								glow.Anchored = false
							end
							self.glows[part] = glow
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end

		for source, shell in pairs(self.parts) do
			if not seen[source] then
				self.faceTextures[shell] = nil
				if self.tints then
					self.tints[shell] = nil
				end
				shell:Destroy()
				self.parts[source] = nil
				if self.glows and self.glows[source] then
					self.glows[source]:Destroy()
					self.glows[source] = nil
				end
			end
		end

	end

	-- Hide body under chams: the real parts are made invisible on your screen only, so only the
	-- cham is seen (with the body showing, clothes and package edges poked through wherever a shell
	-- didn't fully cover it). Done every frame, not only on the rescan, so nothing that resets them
	-- (respawns, other scripts) shows the body again.
	if self.hideSource and self.viewport then
		-- Preview copy: hidden by Transparency (remembered so it can be put back).
		self.hidden = true
		self.viewHidden = self.viewHidden or {}
		for source in pairs(self.parts) do
			if self.viewHidden[source] == nil then
				self.viewHidden[source] = source.Transparency
				source.Transparency = 1
			end
		end
	elseif self.hideSource then
		-- Your own body in first person: the camera hides it, and the shells hide with it.
		local firstPerson = false
		if model == localPlayer.Character then
			local head = model:FindFirstChild("Head")
			firstPerson = head ~= nil and (workspace.CurrentCamera.CFrame.Position - head.Position).Magnitude < 1.5
		end
		local shellModifier = firstPerson and 1 or 0
		self.hidden = true
		for source, shell in pairs(self.parts) do
			if not firstPerson and source.LocalTransparencyModifier ~= 1 then
				source.LocalTransparencyModifier = 1
			end
			if shell.LocalTransparencyModifier ~= shellModifier then
				shell.LocalTransparencyModifier = shellModifier
			end
		end
		for _, glow in pairs(self.glows or {}) do
			if glow.LocalTransparencyModifier ~= shellModifier then
				glow.LocalTransparencyModifier = shellModifier
			end
		end
	elseif self.hidden then
		self:restoreSources()
	end

	-- Preview shells follow their (posed) parts by hand.
	if self.viewport then
		for source, shell in pairs(self.parts) do
			shell.CFrame = source.CFrame
		end
		for source, glow in pairs(self.glows or {}) do
			glow.CFrame = source.CFrame
		end
	end

	-- Your own body hides parts in first person every frame; the shells follow that.
	if model == localPlayer.Character and not self.hideSource then
		for source, glow in pairs(self.glows or {}) do
			if glow.LocalTransparencyModifier ~= source.LocalTransparencyModifier then
				glow.LocalTransparencyModifier = source.LocalTransparencyModifier
			end
		end
		for source, shell in pairs(self.parts) do
			if shell.LocalTransparencyModifier ~= source.LocalTransparencyModifier then
				shell.LocalTransparencyModifier = source.LocalTransparencyModifier
			end
		end
	end
end)

---Turn the shells into a frozen copy where they are now (ghost trails).
function Chams:freeze()
	for _, shell in pairs(self.parts) do
		local weld = shell:FindFirstChildOfClass("WeldConstraint")
		if weld then
			weld:Destroy()
		end
		shell.Anchored = true
	end
	self.model = nil
	-- Ghost copies clean themselves up; the sweep leaves them be.
	self.frozen = true
end

---Draw the chams on `model`. `lookName` picks the material look (defaults to the ESP setting).
Chams.update = LPH_NO_VIRTUALIZE(function(self, model, color, transparency, throughWalls, now, edgeColor, edgeTransparency, lookName)
	if not model then
		return
	end
	-- A character taken out of the world (player left, team menu, respawning) would keep its
	-- shells frozen where it was last seen, so those are cleared instead.
	if not self.viewport and not model:IsDescendantOf(workspace) then
		if self.proxy then
			self:clear()
		end
		return
	end
	now = now or os.clock()
	lookName = lookName or flags.esp_chams_material or "Aura"
	-- "None" means the plain highlight for the ESP chams; anything else using shells gets Aura.
	if lookName == "None" then
		lookName = "Aura"
	end
	local look = Chams.LOOKS[lookName] or Chams.LOOKS.Ropes

	-- Rebuilt when the look or the glow layer setting changes.
	local wantGlow = self.glowEnabled == true
	if self.lookName ~= lookName or self.glowBuilt ~= wantGlow then
		self.lookName = lookName
		self.glowBuilt = wantGlow
		self:clearShells()
	end
	self:sync(model, now, look)

	edgeColor = edgeColor or color:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.35)
	edgeTransparency = math.clamp(edgeTransparency or 0.15, 0, 1)

	-- Each player's animation runs a little out of step with everyone else's.
	self.phase = self.phase or math.random() * math.pi * 2
	local animated = look.rainbow or look.pulse or look.shimmer or look.fade or look.scroll
	-- Animated looks repaint 20 times a second (every frame for every player was wasted work).
	if animated and self.appliedKey and now - (self.animAt or 0) < 1 / 20 then
		return self:updateHighlight(self.lastColor or color, self.lastEdgeColor or edgeColor, edgeTransparency, throughWalls, look)
	end
	self.animAt = now

	-- The rim keeps the chams color you picked, even on looks with their own color (Gold, Void...).
	local rimColor = color
	if look.fixed then
		color = look.fixed
	end
	if look.rainbow then
		color = Color3.fromHSV((now * 0.25 + self.phase * 0.05) % 1, 0.75, 1)
	end
	if look.whiten then
		color = color:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), look.whiten)
	end
	if look.pulse then
		local amount = type(look.pulse) == "number" and look.pulse or 0.35
		color = color:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), (math.sin(now * (look.pulseSpeed or 4) + self.phase) + 1) / 2 * amount)
	end
	if look.shimmer then
		-- A sheen that rolls over and fades: sharper peaks than a plain pulse.
		local wave = (math.sin(now * 2.2 + self.phase) + 1) / 2
		color = color:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), wave * wave * look.shimmer)
	end

	local partTransparency = math.clamp(transparency or 0.1, 0, 0.95)
	if look.minTransparency then
		partTransparency = math.max(partTransparency, look.minTransparency)
	end
	if look.fade then
		partTransparency = math.clamp(partTransparency + (math.sin(now * 2.5) + 1) / 2 * 0.6, 0, 0.95)
	end
	if look.wireframe then
		partTransparency = 1
	end

	-- Only rewrite the shells when the color or transparency actually changed.
	partTransparency = math.floor(partTransparency * 50) / 50
	local key = color:ToHex() .. partTransparency .. edgeColor:ToHex() .. tostring(look.wireframe)
	if key ~= self.appliedKey then
		self.appliedKey = key
		local tint = Vector3.new(color.R, color.G, color.B)
		-- The ESP preview can't draw Neon, ForceField or Glass (they show as plain plastic), so it
		-- gets the closest stand-in: brighter for glowing looks, see-through for force fields and glass.
		local shellColor, shellTransparency = color, partTransparency
		if self.viewport then
			if look.material == Enum.Material.Neon then
				shellColor = color:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.3)
			elseif look.material == Enum.Material.ForceField then
				shellColor = color:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.2)
				shellTransparency = math.max(partTransparency, 0.45)
			elseif look.material == Enum.Material.Glass then
				shellTransparency = math.max(partTransparency, 0.35)
			end
		end
		for _, shell in pairs(self.parts) do
			shell.Color = shellColor
			shell.Transparency = shellTransparency
			local tintMesh = self.tints and self.tints[shell]
			if typeof(tintMesh) == "Instance" then
				tintMesh.VertexColor = tint
			end
			local faces = self.faceTextures[shell]
			if type(faces) == "table" then
				-- The pattern sits a little lighter than the body under it, so it reads as a pattern
				-- in the material instead of white specks over it.
				for _, texture in ipairs(faces) do
					texture.Color3 = color:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.25)
					texture.Transparency = math.clamp(partTransparency + 0.3, 0, 0.95)
				end
			end
			-- Wireframe: highlights skip fully see-through parts, so it drew nothing. Each body
			-- part gets glowing edges instead (they draw through walls too).
			local wire = shell:FindFirstChild("AquaWire")
			if look.wireframe then
				if not wire then
					wire = Instance.new("SelectionBox")
					wire.Name = "AquaWire"
					wire.SurfaceTransparency = 1
					wire.LineThickness = 0.035
					wire.Adornee = shell
					wire.Parent = shell
				end
				wire.Color3 = color
				wire.Transparency = math.clamp(transparency or 0, 0, 0.6)
			elseif wire then
				wire:Destroy()
			end
		end
	end
	self.lastColor, self.lastEdgeColor = color, edgeColor

	-- The rim: a light tint of the chams color that breathes in and out, 20 times a second.
	if self.glows and next(self.glows) and now - (self.rimAt or 0) >= 1 / 20 then
		self.rimAt = now
		local base = look.rainbow and color or rimColor
		local rim = base:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.35)
		local breathe = (math.sin(now * 3 + self.phase) + 1) / 2
		local rimTransparency
		if self.viewport then
			-- The preview draws it as a Neon haze, which has to stay faint.
			rimTransparency = math.clamp(0.78 + partTransparency * 0.15 + breathe * 0.08, 0.75, 0.97)
		else
			rimTransparency = math.clamp(0.1 + partTransparency * 0.5 + breathe * 0.25, 0.05, 0.92)
		end
		rimTransparency = math.floor(rimTransparency * 50) / 50
		for _, glow in pairs(self.glows) do
			if glow.Color ~= rim then
				glow.Color = rim
			end
			if glow.Transparency ~= rimTransparency then
				glow.Transparency = rimTransparency
			end
		end
	end

	-- Moving surfaces: the pattern on each body block slides along (liquid metal flows, lava
	-- creeps, matrix code rains down, stars drift). Textures tile every 2 studs, so it wraps.
	if look.scroll then
		local tile = look.tile or 2
		local u = (now * look.scroll.X + self.phase) % tile
		local v = (now * look.scroll.Y + self.phase) % tile
		for _, faces in pairs(self.faceTextures) do
			if type(faces) == "table" then
				for _, texture in ipairs(faces) do
					texture.OffsetStudsU = u
					texture.OffsetStudsV = v
				end
			end
		end
	end

	self:updateHighlight(color, edgeColor, edgeTransparency, throughWalls, look)
end)

---The outline (and through-walls fill) around the shells.
Chams.updateHighlight = LPH_NO_VIRTUALIZE(function(self, color, edgeColor, edgeTransparency, throughWalls, look)
	-- The highlight is only written when something about it changed: re-setting the same values
	-- every frame still makes Roblox redo the highlight, for every player.
	local highlight = self.highlight
	if not highlight then
		return
	end
	-- Highlights don't draw inside a viewport (the ESP preview).
	if self.viewport then
		if highlight.Enabled then
			highlight.Enabled = false
		end
		return
	end
	-- Wireframe has nothing for a highlight to draw (and Roblox only shows 31 at once).
	if look.wireframe then
		if highlight.Enabled then
			highlight.Enabled = false
		end
		return
	end
	local fillTransparency = throughWalls and 0.75 or 1
	local outline = math.floor(edgeTransparency * 50) / 50
	local highlightKey = color:ToHex() .. edgeColor:ToHex() .. fillTransparency .. outline .. tostring(throughWalls)
	if highlight.Adornee ~= self.proxy then
		highlight.Adornee = self.proxy
		self.highlightKey = nil
	end
	if not highlight.Enabled then
		highlight.Enabled = true
	end
	if self.highlightKey ~= highlightKey then
		self.highlightKey = highlightKey
		highlight.FillColor = color
		-- A faint fill only matters through walls; in plain view the material shows as is.
		highlight.FillTransparency = fillTransparency
		highlight.OutlineColor = edgeColor
		highlight.OutlineTransparency = outline
		highlight.DepthMode = throughWalls and Enum.HighlightDepthMode.AlwaysOnTop or Enum.HighlightDepthMode.Occluded
	end
end)

function Chams:destroy()
	self:unwatch()
	self:restoreSources()
	if self.highlight then
		self.highlight:Destroy()
	end
	if self.proxy then
		self.proxy:Destroy()
	end
	self.proxy = nil
	self.parts = {}
	self.faceTextures = {}
	self.model = nil
end

function Chams:clear()
	self:unwatch()
	self:restoreSources()
	if self.highlight then
		self.highlight.Enabled = false
		self.highlight.Adornee = nil
	end
	if self.proxy then
		self.proxy:Destroy()
		self.proxy = nil
	end
	self.parts = {}
	self.faceTextures = {}
	self.model = nil
	self.state = nil
	self.appliedKey = nil
end

-- Adornment chams (the "adornment", "wireframe" and "image" chams types): handle adornments
-- drawn on the player's real body parts, so they show through walls. Built once per character
-- and type, then only recolored when the colors change.
-- Everything hangs off this one table: the file's top level is at Luau's 200-local limit.
local AdornChams = {}
AdornChams.__index = AdornChams

AdornChams.folder = Instance.new("Folder")
AdornChams.folder.Name = ""
AdornChams.folder.Parent = coreGui
onUnload(function()
	AdornChams.folder:Destroy()
end)

AdornChams.HALF_PI = math.pi / 2
AdornChams.resolving = {}

function AdornChams.new()
	return setmetatable({ character = nil, kind = nil, image = nil, parts = {}, key = nil }, AdornChams)
end

---Remove every adornment.
function AdornChams:clear()
	for _, entry in pairs(self.parts) do
		for _, adornment in ipairs(entry.all) do
			adornment:Destroy()
		end
	end
	table.clear(self.parts)
	if self.billboard then
		self.billboard:Destroy()
		self.billboard, self.picture = nil, nil
	end
	self.character, self.kind, self.image, self.key = nil, nil, nil, nil
end

---The parts worth drawing: body parts and accessories, not the root or held tools.
function AdornChams.adornParts(character, bodyOnly)
	local list = {}
	for _, part in ipairs(character:GetDescendants()) do
		if part:IsA("BasePart") and part.Name ~= "HumanoidRootPart" and part.Transparency < 0.99
			and not part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Tool")
			and not (bodyOnly and part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Accessory")) then
			table.insert(list, part)
		end
	end
	return list
end

---A part's wireframe mesh: every face split into a grid of about half-stud squares, each square
---cut into two triangles, like a 3D model's wireframe.
function AdornChams.wireMesh(size)
	local x, y, z = size.X / 2, size.Y / 2, size.Z / 2
	local lines = {}
	---One face: a corner, two edge vectors, and how many cells along each.
	local function face(origin, u, v)
		local nu = math.clamp(math.floor(u.Magnitude / 0.5 + 0.5), 1, 8)
		local nv = math.clamp(math.floor(v.Magnitude / 0.5 + 0.5), 1, 8)
		for i = 0, nu do
			local start = origin + u * (i / nu)
			table.insert(lines, { start, start + v })
		end
		for j = 0, nv do
			local start = origin + v * (j / nv)
			table.insert(lines, { start, start + u })
		end
		for i = 0, nu + NEG_ONE do
			for j = 0, nv + NEG_ONE do
				local corner = origin + u * (i / nu) + v * (j / nv)
				table.insert(lines, { corner, corner + u / nu + v / nv })
			end
		end
	end
	local low = Vector3.new(x * NEG_ONE, y * NEG_ONE, z * NEG_ONE)
	local alongX, alongY, alongZ = Vector3.new(size.X, 0, 0), Vector3.new(0, size.Y, 0), Vector3.new(0, 0, size.Z)
	face(low, alongX, alongZ)
	face(low + alongY, alongX, alongZ)
	face(low, alongX, alongY)
	face(low + alongZ, alongX, alongY)
	face(low, alongZ, alongY)
	face(low + alongX, alongZ, alongY)
	return lines
end


---Build the adornments for one part.
function AdornChams:addPart(part)
	local entry = { all = {}, size = part.Size }
	local kind = self.kind
	if kind == "adornment" then
		local box = Instance.new("BoxHandleAdornment")
		box.Name = ""
		box.Adornee = part
		-- A hair bigger than the part, so it never flickers against the body's surface.
		box.Size = part.Size * 1.04
		box.ZIndex = 1
		box.Parent = AdornChams.folder
		entry.box = box
		table.insert(entry.all, box)
	end
	if kind == "adornment" then
		local outline = Instance.new("SelectionBox")
		outline.Name = ""
		outline.Adornee = part
		outline.LineThickness = 0.025
		outline.SurfaceTransparency = 1
		outline.Parent = AdornChams.folder
		entry.outline = outline
		table.insert(entry.all, outline)
	elseif kind == "wireframe" then
		-- Lines only: a triangle mesh over every face of the limb, like a 3D wireframe render.
		-- The lines are added when it's colored (see recolor).
		local wire = Instance.new("WireframeHandleAdornment")
		wire.Name = ""
		wire.Adornee = part
		wire.Thickness = 1
		wire.Parent = AdornChams.folder
		entry.wire = wire
		table.insert(entry.all, wire)
	end
	self.parts[part] = entry
end

---Image chams: a billboard on the root part, sized to the body (feet to the top of the head)
---so the picture stands in for the whole player.
AdornChams.updateImage = LPH_NO_VIRTUALIZE(function(self, character, image, transparency, throughWalls)
	local root = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	local head = character:FindFirstChild("Head")
	if not (root and head) or image == "" then
		if self.billboard then
			self.billboard.Enabled = false
		end
		return
	end
	local billboard = self.billboard
	if not billboard then
		billboard = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
		billboard.Name = ""
		billboard.LightInfluence = 0
		billboard.ResetOnSpawn = false
		local picture = Instance.new("ImageLabel")
		picture.Name = ""
		picture.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
		picture.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		picture.ScaleType = Enum.ScaleType.Stretch
		picture.Parent = billboard
		billboard.Parent = AdornChams.folder
		self.billboard = billboard
		self.picture = picture
	end
	-- Body height: from the feet (root height plus hip height below the root) to the head top.
	local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	local below = root.Size.Y / 2 + (humanoid and humanoid.HipHeight > 0.1 and humanoid.HipHeight or 2)
	local above = (head.Position.Y + head.Size.Y / 2) + NEG_ONE * root.Position.Y
	local height = math.clamp(below + above, 3, 9)
	local width = height * 0.55
	if billboard.Adornee ~= root then
		billboard.Adornee = root
	end
	billboard.Size = UDim2.fromScale(width, height)
	billboard.StudsOffset = Vector3.new(0, (above + NEG_ONE * below) / 2, 0)
	billboard.AlwaysOnTop = throughWalls
	billboard.Enabled = true
	if self.picture.Image ~= image then
		self.picture.Image = image
	end
	self.picture.ImageTransparency = transparency
end)

---Draw (or recolor) this character's adornment chams.
AdornChams.update = LPH_NO_VIRTUALIZE(function(self, character, kind, image, fillColor, fillTransparency, edgeColor, edgeTransparency, throughWalls)
	if self.character ~= character or self.kind ~= kind or (kind == "image" and self.image ~= image) then
		self:clear()
		self.character, self.kind, self.image = character, kind, image
		self.scannedAt = nil
	end
	-- New parts (respawned limbs, accessories) get adornments; removed or resized ones are redone.
	-- Image: one picture of the whole player, head to toe, always facing you.
	if kind == "image" then
		return self:updateImage(character, image, fillTransparency, throughWalls)
	end
	-- Re-checked twice a second: scanning every character's parts every frame was most of the
	-- cost of these chams types.
	local now = os.clock()
	if self.scannedAt and now - self.scannedAt < 0.5 then
		return self:recolor(fillColor, fillTransparency, edgeColor, edgeTransparency, throughWalls)
	end
	-- Spread out so every player's rescan doesn't land on the same frame.
	self.scannedAt = now + math.random() * 0.15
	-- Wireframe draws the body only (hats would just be wire boxes).
	local parts = AdornChams.adornParts(character, kind == "wireframe")
	local current = {}
	for _, part in ipairs(parts) do
		current[part] = true
		local entry = self.parts[part]
		if entry and entry.size ~= part.Size then
			for _, adornment in ipairs(entry.all) do
				adornment:Destroy()
			end
			self.parts[part] = nil
			entry = nil
		end
		if not entry then
			self:addPart(part)
			self.key = nil
		end
	end
	for part, entry in pairs(self.parts) do
		if not current[part] then
			for _, adornment in ipairs(entry.all) do
				adornment:Destroy()
			end
			self.parts[part] = nil
		end
	end
	self:recolor(fillColor, fillTransparency, edgeColor, edgeTransparency, throughWalls)
end)

---Apply colors to the adornments (only when they changed).
AdornChams.recolor = LPH_NO_VIRTUALIZE(function(self, fillColor, fillTransparency, edgeColor, edgeTransparency, throughWalls)
	local kind = self.kind
	local key = fillColor:ToHex() .. edgeColor:ToHex() .. math.floor(fillTransparency * 100) .. math.floor(edgeTransparency * 100) .. tostring(throughWalls)
	if self.key == key then
		return
	end
	self.key = key
	for _, entry in pairs(self.parts) do
		if entry.box then
			entry.box.Color3 = fillColor
			entry.box.Transparency = fillTransparency
			entry.box.AlwaysOnTop = throughWalls
		end
		if entry.outline then
			entry.outline.Color3 = edgeColor
			entry.outline.Transparency = edgeTransparency
			entry.outline.Visible = edgeTransparency < 1
		end
		-- Wireframe lines in the chams color; the transparency slider fades them. A line keeps
		-- the color it was added with (changing Color3 later doesn't repaint it, which left every
		-- wireframe the default blue), so the lines are redrawn whenever the color changes.
		if entry.wire then
			if entry.wireColor ~= fillColor then
				entry.wireColor = fillColor
				entry.wire:Clear()
				entry.wire.Color3 = fillColor
				for _, line in ipairs(AdornChams.wireMesh(entry.size)) do
					entry.wire:AddLine(line[1], line[2])
				end
			end
			entry.wire.Transparency = fillTransparency * 0.6
			entry.wire.AlwaysOnTop = throughWalls
		end
	end
end)


---Current US Eastern time (UTC-5, or UTC-4 during daylight saving), e.g. "1:49:10 PM EST".
---DST runs from the 2nd Sunday of March 2 AM to the 1st Sunday of November 2 AM, local time.
---@return string
local function getEasternTime()
	local now = os.time()
	local year = tonumber(os.date("!%Y", now))

	-- Roblox's os.time(table) reads the table as UTC.
	local function nthSunday(month, n)
		local weekday = os.date("!*t", os.time({ year = year, month = month, day = 1, hour = 12 })).wday
		return 1 + (8 - weekday) % 7 + (n - 1) * 7
	end

	local dstStart = os.time({ year = year, month = 3, day = nthSunday(3, 2), hour = 7 })
	local dstEnd = os.time({ year = year, month = 11, day = nthSunday(11, 1), hour = 6 })
	local daylight = now >= dstStart and now < dstEnd
	local eastern = now + (daylight and -4 or -5) * 3600

	local clock = os.date("!%I:%M:%S %p", eastern):gsub("^0", "")
	return clock .. (daylight and " EDT" or " EST")
end

---Hue that cycles over time, shared by every rainbow option.
---@param speed number cycles per second
---@param offset number?
---@return Color3
local function getRainbow(speed, offset)
	return Color3.fromHSV(((os.clock() * speed) + (offset or 0)) % 1, 0.7, 1)
end

---Current accent color, falling back to the library default.
---@return Color3
local function getAccent()
	if flags.theme_rainbow then
		return getRainbow(flags.theme_rainbow_speed or 0.15)
	end

	return flags.theme_accent and flags.theme_accent.Color or Color3.fromRGB(100, 100, 255)
end

-- Water look: a band of deep, mid and light foam shades of the theme color that drifts across
-- and sways like a wave.
-- Any UIGradient added here is animated together, 30 times a second. (Kept on Hooks: the top
-- level is at Luau's 200-local limit.)
Hooks.water = {
	gradients = {},
	colors = ColorSequence.new({
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, Color3.fromRGB(18, 70, 190)),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.3, Color3.fromRGB(35, 160, 255)),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, Color3.fromRGB(175, 238, 255)),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.7, Color3.fromRGB(35, 160, 255)),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, Color3.fromRGB(18, 70, 190)),
	}),
	-- Brighter version for small text over the game (the deep shade made it unreadable).
	lightColors = ColorSequence.new({
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, Color3.fromRGB(110, 190, 255)),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, Color3.new(1, 1, 1)),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, Color3.fromRGB(110, 190, 255)),
	}),
	light = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" }),
	updatedAt = 0,
}

---Start animating a gradient with the water look (`phase` staggers different texts; `light` uses
---the brighter colors).
function Hooks.water.add(gradient, phase, light)
	Hooks.water.light[gradient] = light == true or nil
	gradient.Color = light and Hooks.water.lightColors or Hooks.water.colors
	gradient.Enabled = true
	Hooks.water.gradients[gradient] = phase or 0
end

---Stop animating a gradient (its owner sets its own colors back).
function Hooks.water.remove(gradient)
	Hooks.water.gradients[gradient] = nil
end

library:connection(runService.Heartbeat, function()
	local now = os.clock()
	-- Optimize Mode: the water look stays still (no per-frame gradient writes).
	if now - Hooks.water.updatedAt < 1 / 30 or flags.optimize_mode == true then
		return
	end
	Hooks.water.updatedAt = now
	-- The water takes the theme color: a deep shade of it, the color itself, and a light foam.
	local accent = getAccent()
	local recolor = Hooks.water.accent ~= accent
	if recolor then
		Hooks.water.accent = accent
		local deep = accent:Lerp(Color3.new(0, 0, 0), 0.5)
		local foam = accent:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.72)
		Hooks.water.colors = ColorSequence.new({
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, deep),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.3, accent),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, foam),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.7, accent),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, deep),
		})
		local bright = accent:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.45)
		Hooks.water.lightColors = ColorSequence.new({
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, bright),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, Color3.new(1, 1, 1)),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, bright),
		})
	end
	for gradient, phase in pairs(Hooks.water.gradients) do
		if not gradient.Parent then
			Hooks.water.gradients[gradient] = nil
		else
			if recolor then
				gradient.Color = Hooks.water.light[gradient] and Hooks.water.lightColors or Hooks.water.colors
			end
			local wave = math.sin(now * 1.3 + phase)
			-- The bright foam band sweeps across over and over, tilting with the wave.
			gradient.Offset = Vector2.new((now * 0.35 + phase) % 2 + NEG_ONE, wave * 0.08)
			gradient.Rotation = wave * 12
		end
	end
end)

-- Text animations: one engine for every animated text (menu title, menu logo, ESP names / flags /
-- tags / health number, FOV self flags). Each label gets a UIGradient registered under a group and
-- the group's dropdown picks the look. Gradients multiply the text color, so rich-text colors
-- (tags, the accent "lab") keep their hue under every style.
Hooks.textFx = {
	STYLES = { "None", "Water", "Shimmer", "Rainbow", "Gradient", "Fade", "Flash", "Pulse", "Breathe", "Wave", "Reveal", "Glitch" },
	-- Strong keys: an Instance's Lua reference can be collected while the Instance lives, which
	-- silently dropped every ESP label. Entries are pruned once their gradient loses its parent.
	entries = {},
	-- Which flag holds each group's style, and its default.
	groups = {
		menu = { flag = "text_anim_menu", default = "Water" },
		esp_name = { flag = "esp_text_anim_name", default = "None" },
		esp_flags = { flag = "esp_text_anim_flags", default = "None" },
		esp_tags = { flag = "esp_text_anim_tags", default = "None" },
		esp_health = { flag = "esp_text_anim_health", default = "None" },
		fov_flags = { flag = "self_flags_anim", default = "Shimmer" },
	},
	updatedAt = 0,
	SOLID = NumberSequence.new(0),
	white = ColorSequence.new(Color3.new(1, 1, 1)),
}

---Animate a gradient under a group (`light` keeps Water bright for colored / small text).
---@param gradient UIGradient
---@param group string
---@param phase number?
---@param light boolean?
function Hooks.textFx.add(gradient, group, phase, light)
	Hooks.textFx.entries[gradient] = { group = group, phase = phase or math.random() * 3, light = light == true }
end

---Stop animating a gradient and turn it off.
---@param gradient UIGradient
function Hooks.textFx.remove(gradient)
	Hooks.textFx.entries[gradient] = nil
	gradient.Enabled = false
end

---Make a label's animation gradient and register it.
---@param label GuiObject
---@param group string
---@param light boolean?
---@return UIGradient
function Hooks.textFx.attach(label, group, light)
	local gradient = Instance.new("UIGradient")
	gradient.Name = ""
	gradient.Enabled = false
	gradient.Parent = label
	Hooks.textFx.add(gradient, group, nil, light)
	return gradient
end

---The style a group is set to right now.
---@param group string
---@return string
function Hooks.textFx.styleOf(group)
	local config = Hooks.textFx.groups[group]
	if not config then
		return "None"
	end
	-- The menu's text follows the "text animations" master toggle.
	if group == "menu" and flags.water_text == false then
		return "None"
	end
	return flags[config.flag] or config.default
end

-- Styles that paint their own colors. A gradient only multiplies the text color, so on team colored
-- names or red / yellow tags these were invisible; under them the text is drawn white instead.
Hooks.textFx.RECOLOR = { Water = true, Rainbow = true, Gradient = true, Fade = true, Flash = true }

---The text color a label should use under its group's style.
---@param group string
---@param color Color3
---@return Color3
function Hooks.textFx.tint(group, color)
	return Hooks.textFx.RECOLOR[Hooks.textFx.styleOf(group)] and Color3.new(1, 1, 1) or color
end

---Rich text with every font color turned white when the group's style paints its own colors.
---@param group string
---@param text string
---@return string
function Hooks.textFx.tintText(group, text)
	if not Hooks.textFx.RECOLOR[Hooks.textFx.styleOf(group)] then
		return text
	end
	return (string.gsub(text, 'color="#%x+"', 'color="#FFFFFF"'))
end

---The two colors the two-color styles (Gradient / Fade / Flash) use.
---@return Color3, Color3
function Hooks.textFx.colors()
	local first = flags.text_anim_color1 and flags.text_anim_color1.Color or Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	local second = flags.text_anim_theme ~= false and getAccent()
		or (flags.text_anim_color2 and flags.text_anim_color2.Color or Color3.fromRGB(120, 80, 255))
	return first, second
end

---One tick's shared look for a style (sequences built once, every gradient reuses them).
---@param style string
---@param light boolean
---@param t number scaled time
---@return table
function Hooks.textFx.build(style, light, t)
	local white = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	local first, second = Hooks.textFx.colors()
	if style == "Water" then
		return { color = light and Hooks.water.lightColors or Hooks.water.colors, sweep = 0.35, range = 2, water = true }
	elseif style == "Shimmer" then
		local dim = Color3.new(0.6, 0.6, 0.6)
		Hooks.textFx.shimmer = Hooks.textFx.shimmer or ColorSequence.new({
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, dim),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.4, dim),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, white),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.6, dim),
			ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, dim),
		})
		return { color = Hooks.textFx.shimmer, sweep = 0.6, range = 2.4, rotation = 15 }
	elseif style == "Rainbow" then
		local points = {}
		for index = 0, 6 do
			local position = index / 6
			points[index + 1] = ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(position, Color3.fromHSV((position * 0.6 + t * 0.25) % 1, 0.6, 1))
		end
		return { color = ColorSequence.new(points) }
	elseif style == "Gradient" then
		local points = {}
		for index = 0, 6 do
			local position = index / 6
			points[index + 1] = ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(position, first:Lerp(second, (math.sin((position * 2 + NEG_ONE * t) * math.pi) + 1) / 2))
		end
		return { color = ColorSequence.new(points) }
	elseif style == "Fade" then
		return { color = ColorSequence.new(first:Lerp(second, (math.sin(t * 3) + 1) / 2)) }
	elseif style == "Flash" then
		return { color = ColorSequence.new(math.floor(t * 3) % 2 == 0 and first or second) }
	elseif style == "Pulse" then
		return { color = ColorSequence.new(white:Lerp(Color3.new(0.45, 0.45, 0.45), (math.sin(t * 4) + 1) / 2)) }
	elseif style == "Breathe" then
		return { transparency = NumberSequence.new(math.floor((math.sin(t * 2.5) + 1) * 30) / 100) }
	elseif style == "Wave" then
		Hooks.textFx.wave = Hooks.textFx.wave or NumberSequence.new({
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.35, 0),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, 0.75),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.65, 0),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0),
		})
		return { transparency = Hooks.textFx.wave, sweep = 0.5, range = 2.4 }
	elseif style == "Reveal" then
		Hooks.textFx.reveal = Hooks.textFx.reveal or NumberSequence.new({
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.45, 0),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.55, 1),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
		})
		return { transparency = Hooks.textFx.reveal, reveal = true }
	elseif style == "Glitch" then
		return { glitch = true }
	end
	return {}
end

library:connection(runService.Heartbeat, function()
	local fx = Hooks.textFx
	local now = os.clock()
	-- Optimize Mode: animated text holds still.
	if now - fx.updatedAt < 1 / 30 or flags.optimize_mode == true then
		return
	end
	fx.updatedAt = now
	local t = now * (flags.text_anim_speed or 1)
	local looks = {}
	local styles = {}
	for gradient, entry in pairs(fx.entries) do
		if not gradient.Parent then
			fx.entries[gradient] = nil
		else
			fx.step(gradient, entry, styles, looks, t)
		end
	end
end)

---Move one animated gradient a tick forward.
function Hooks.textFx.step(gradient, entry, styles, looks, t)
	local fx = Hooks.textFx
	do
		local style = styles[entry.group]
		if not style then
			style = fx.styleOf(entry.group)
			styles[entry.group] = style
		end
		if style == "None" then
			if entry.style ~= "None" then
				entry.style = "None"
				gradient.Enabled = false
			end
			return
		end
		local key = style .. (entry.light and "+" or "")
		local look = looks[key]
		if not look then
			look = fx.build(style, entry.light, t)
			looks[key] = look
		end
		if entry.style ~= style then
			entry.style = style
			entry.color, entry.transparency = nil, nil
			gradient.Enabled = true
			gradient.Offset = Vector2.zero
			gradient.Rotation = 0
		end

		local color = look.color or fx.white
		if look.glitch then
			-- Mostly still, with short random bursts of a shifted, off-color slice.
			local burst = math.random() < 0.05
			color = burst and ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromHSV(math.random(), 0.7, 1), Color3.new(1, 1, 1)) or fx.white
			gradient.Offset = burst and Vector2.new(math.random() * 0.6 + NEG_ONE * 0.3, 0) or Vector2.zero
			gradient.Rotation = burst and math.random(0, 40) or 0
		end
		if entry.color ~= color then
			entry.color = color
			gradient.Color = color
		end
		local transparency = look.transparency or fx.SOLID
		if entry.transparency ~= transparency then
			entry.transparency = transparency
			gradient.Transparency = transparency
		end

		local phase = entry.phase
		if look.water then
			local wave = math.sin(t * 1.3 + phase)
			gradient.Offset = Vector2.new((t * look.sweep + phase) % look.range + NEG_ONE, wave * 0.08)
			gradient.Rotation = wave * 12
		elseif look.sweep then
			gradient.Offset = Vector2.new((t * look.sweep + phase) % look.range + NEG_ONE * look.range / 2, 0)
			gradient.Rotation = look.rotation or 0
		elseif look.reveal then
			-- Types in left to right, holds, then starts over.
			local progress = math.min(((t * 0.45 + phase) % 1.6) / 1.1, 1)
			gradient.Offset = Vector2.new(progress * 1.1 + NEG_ONE * 0.55, 0)
		end
	end
end

---Current font color, falling back to the library default.
---@return Color3
local function getTextColor()
	return flags.theme_text and flags.theme_text.Color or Color3.fromRGB(170, 170, 170)
end

---Create a styled text label for overlay panels.
---@param parent Instance
---@param text string
---@return TextLabel
local function createOverlayText(parent, text)
	return library:create("TextLabel", {
		Parent = parent,
		Name = "",
		FontFace = currentFont,
		RichText = true,
		Text = text,
		TextSize = 12,
		TextColor3 = getTextColor(),
		TextStrokeTransparency = 0.5,
		TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		BorderSizePixel = 0,
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 14),
		AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.X,
	})
end

---Drag a panel with a finger or the mouse. Roblox's built-in Draggable ignores touch, and on
---phones the menu's gui is shrunk by a UIScale, so screen movement is divided back by it.
local function makeDraggable(frame)
	frame.Draggable = false
	local dragStart, frameStart = nil, nil
	frame.InputBegan:Connect(function(input)
		if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
			dragStart = Vector2.new(input.Position.X, input.Position.Y)
			frameStart = frame.Position
		end
	end)
	library:connection(userInputService.InputChanged, function(input)
		if not dragStart or (input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement and input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Touch) then
			return
		end
		local guiScale = library.gui:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
		local scale = guiScale and math.max(guiScale.Scale, 0.05) or 1
		local delta = (Vector2.new(input.Position.X, input.Position.Y) - dragStart) / scale
		frame.Position = UDim2.new(frameStart.X.Scale, frameStart.X.Offset + delta.X, frameStart.Y.Scale, frameStart.Y.Offset + delta.Y)
	end)
	library:connection(userInputService.InputEnded, function(input)
		if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
			dragStart = nil
		end
	end)
end

---Build a draggable vaderpaste-style panel that auto-sizes around its content.
---@param position UDim2
---@return Frame, Frame
local function createOverlay(position)
	local holder = library:create("Frame", {
		Parent = library.gui,
		Name = "",
		Position = position,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0),
		AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY,
		Active = true,
		ZIndex = 2,
	})
	makeDraggable(holder)

	-- Borders are UIStrokes (drawn evenly on every side) instead of BorderSizePixel, which
	-- sits outside the frame and left the accent line one pixel off on each side.
	local outer = library:create("Frame", {
		Parent = holder,
		Name = "",
		BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(40, 40, 40),
		BorderSizePixel = 0,
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0),
		AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY,
		ZIndex = 2,
	})
	library:create("UIStroke", { Parent = outer, Color = Color3.new(0, 0, 0), LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Miter })

	library:create("UIPadding", {
		Parent = outer,
		PaddingTop = UDim.new(0, 4),
		PaddingBottom = UDim.new(0, 2),
		PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0, 2),
		PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, 2),
	})

	local content = library:create("Frame", {
		Parent = outer,
		Name = "",
		BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(22, 22, 22),
		BorderSizePixel = 0,
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0),
		AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY,
		ZIndex = 2,
	})
	library:create("UIStroke", { Parent = content, Color = Color3.fromRGB(57, 57, 57), LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Miter })

	library:create("UIPadding", {
		Parent = content,
		PaddingTop = UDim.new(0, 4),
		PaddingBottom = UDim.new(0, 4),
		PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0, 8),
		PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, 8),
	})

	library:create("UIListLayout", {
		Parent = content,
		SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder,
		Padding = UDim.new(0, 2),
	})

	-- The accent line and background decal live beside the panel (not inside it) and are
	-- sized in pixels from it, so they never hold the panel open when its content shrinks.
	local accentLine = library:create("Frame", {
		Parent = holder,
		Name = "",
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 2),
		BorderSizePixel = 0,
		ZIndex = 4,
		BackgroundColor3 = getAccent(),
	})
	library:apply_theme(accentLine, "accent", "BackgroundColor3")

	local glow = library:create("ImageLabel", {
		Parent = accentLine,
		Name = "",
		Image = GLOW_IMAGE,
		ImageColor3 = getAccent(),
		ImageTransparency = 0.9,
		ScaleType = Enum.ScaleType.Slice,
		SliceCenter = Rect.new(Vector2.new(21, 21), Vector2.new(79, 79)),
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Position = UDim2.new(0, -20, 0, -20),
		Size = UDim2.new(1, 40, 0, 42),
		ZIndex = 3,
	})
	library:apply_theme(glow, "accent", "ImageColor3")

	-- Optional background decal (Settings > Background), drawn under the panel.
	local background = library:create("ImageLabel", {
		Parent = holder,
		Name = "",
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		ScaleType = Enum.ScaleType.Crop,
		Image = "",
		ZIndex = 1,
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0),
	})

	local function fitToPanel()
		local size = outer.AbsoluteSize
		accentLine.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(size.X, 2)
		background.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(size.X, size.Y)
	end

	fitToPanel()
	library:connection(outer:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"), fitToPanel)
	table.insert(overlayPanels, { holder = holder, image = background })

	return holder, content
end

---Whether an input matches a keybind key (KeyCode or mouse button).
---@param key any
---@param input InputObject
---@return boolean
local function matchesKey(key, input)
	if typeof(key) ~= "EnumItem" then
		return false
	end

	return input.KeyCode == key or input.UserInputType == key
end

---Short display name for a bound key.
---@param key any
---@return string
local function getKeyName(key)
	if typeof(key) ~= "EnumItem" then
		return "none"
	end

	return string.lower(key.Name)
end

---Flip a feature on or off and keep the library toggle in sync.
---@param feature table
---@param enabled boolean
local function setFeature(feature, enabled)
	if flags[feature.flag] == enabled then
		return
	end

	feature.toggle.enabled = enabled
	feature.toggle.set(enabled)
end

---Register a toggle with an attached keybind so it shows in the keybind list.
---Use this for every new feature.
---@param section table
---@param options table
---@return table
local function addFeature(section, options)
	local feature = {
		name = options.name,
		flag = options.flag,
		bindFlag = options.flag .. "_bind",
		lastKey = nil,
		-- Default-on options (like Box) set this false so they don't sit in the list forever.
		listActive = options.listActive,
	}

	feature.toggle = section:toggle({
		name = options.name,
		flag = options.flag,
		default = options.default or false,
		callback = function(enabled)
			-- Keep the library's click state in sync when configs set the toggle.
			if feature.toggle then
				feature.toggle.enabled = enabled
			end

			if options.callback then
				options.callback(enabled)
			end

			-- "Invisible enabled" / "Invisible disabled" once the script has finished loading,
			-- so configs and startup defaults don't spam notifications.
			local changed = feature.lastState ~= nil and feature.lastState ~= enabled
			feature.lastState = enabled == true
			if changed and featureNotificationsReady and flags.feature_notifications ~= false then
				library:notification({ text = feature.name .. (enabled and " enabled" or " disabled"), time = 2 })
			end

			if refreshKeybindList then
				refreshKeybindList()
			end
		end,
	})

	-- Rage features get a red label so they stand out from the legit ones.
	if options.rage then
		local label
		for _, object in ipairs(section.holder and section.holder:GetDescendants() or {}) do
			if (object:IsA("TextButton") or object:IsA("TextLabel")) and string.lower(object.Text) == string.lower(options.name) then
				label = object
			end
		end

		if label then
			local function paint()
				-- Premium-locked rage features stay gray instead of red.
				local wanted = Hooks.premium.locked[label] and DULL_TEXT or RAGE_TEXT
				if label.TextColor3 ~= wanted then
					label.TextColor3 = wanted
				end
			end
			paint()
			library:connection(label:GetPropertyChangedSignal("TextColor3"), paint)
		end
	end

	-- The library's own keybind handler shares one global, so input is handled below instead.
	section:keybind({
		flag = feature.bindFlag,
		mode = "toggle",
		callback = function() end,
	})

	table.insert(features, feature)

	return feature
end

-- Window.
local window = library:window({
	name = " ",
	size = UDim2.fromOffset(600, 740),
})

local windowFrame = library.main_frame[1]
local windowInner = windowFrame:FindFirstChildOfClass("Frame")
Hooks.window = window

-- Side panels (player profile, ESP preview, glow) get their own gui: anything that changes inside
-- the menu's gui makes Roblox redraw the whole menu, so live-updating extras live beside it.
Hooks.sideGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
Hooks.sideGui.Name = ""
Hooks.sideGui.ResetOnSpawn = false
Hooks.sideGui.IgnoreGuiInset = library.gui.IgnoreGuiInset
Hooks.sideGui.DisplayOrder = library.gui.DisplayOrder
Hooks.sideGui.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling
Hooks.sideGui:SetAttribute("AquaLabs", true)
Hooks.sideGui.Parent = coreGui
library:connection(library.gui:GetPropertyChangedSignal("DisplayOrder"), function()
	Hooks.sideGui.DisplayOrder = library.gui.DisplayOrder
end)
library:connection(windowFrame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"), function()
	Hooks.sideGui.Enabled = windowFrame.Visible
end)
onUnload(function()
	Hooks.sideGui:Destroy()
end)

---Whether the mouse is over the open menu or one of its side panels (ESP preview, player
---profile). The FOV circle, crosshairs and the game's gun cursor hide there so they don't sit on
---top of the menu.
function Hooks.mouseOverMenu()
	if not windowFrame.Visible then
		return false
	end
	local mouse = userInputService:GetMouseLocation()
	if not library.gui.IgnoreGuiInset then
		mouse -= game:GetService("GuiService"):GetGuiInset()
	end
	local function over(object)
		local position, size = object.AbsolutePosition, object.AbsoluteSize
		return mouse.X >= position.X and mouse.Y >= position.Y and mouse.X <= position.X + size.X and mouse.Y <= position.Y + size.Y
	end
	if over(windowFrame) then
		return true
	end
	for _, panel in ipairs(Hooks.sideGui:GetChildren()) do
		if panel:IsA("GuiObject") and panel.Visible and over(panel) then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- The game's own crosshair over the menu: the gun cursor (the mouse icon) goes back to a normal
-- pointer, the mouse is shown, and any crosshair the game draws in its gui is hidden. Everything
-- goes back the moment the mouse leaves the menu.
do
	local mouse = localPlayer:GetMouse()
	local hidden = { icon = nil, iconEnabled = nil, guis = {} }
	local crosshairs, scannedAt = {}, 0

	---The game's crosshair guis (anything named like a crosshair), looked up every 2 seconds.
	local function gameCrosshairs()
		local now = os.clock()
		if now - scannedAt < 2 then
			return crosshairs
		end
		scannedAt = now
		table.clear(crosshairs)
		local playerGui = localPlayer:FindFirstChildOfClass("PlayerGui")
		for _, object in ipairs(playerGui and playerGui:GetDescendants() or {}) do
			if object:IsA("GuiObject") and string.find(string.lower(object.Name), "crosshair", 1, true) then
				table.insert(crosshairs, object)
			end
		end
		return crosshairs
	end

	local function restore()
		if hidden.icon ~= nil then
			if mouse.Icon == "" then
				mouse.Icon = hidden.icon
			end
			hidden.icon = nil
		end
		if hidden.iconEnabled ~= nil then
			userInputService.MouseIconEnabled = hidden.iconEnabled
			hidden.iconEnabled = nil
		end
		for object in pairs(hidden.guis) do
			if object.Parent then
				object.Visible = true
			end
		end
		table.clear(hidden.guis)
	end

	library:connection(runService.RenderStepped, function()
		if not Hooks.mouseOverMenu() then
			if hidden.icon ~= nil or hidden.iconEnabled ~= nil or next(hidden.guis) then
				restore()
			end
			return
		end
		if mouse.Icon ~= "" then
			hidden.icon = mouse.Icon
			mouse.Icon = ""
		end
		-- The menu's custom cursor hides the mouse on purpose; otherwise show the pointer.
		if not flags.custom_cursor and not userInputService.MouseIconEnabled then
			hidden.iconEnabled = hidden.iconEnabled == nil and false or hidden.iconEnabled
			userInputService.MouseIconEnabled = true
		end
		for _, object in ipairs(gameCrosshairs()) do
			if object.Parent and object.Visible then
				hidden.guis[object] = true
				object.Visible = false
			end
		end
	end)
	onUnload(restore)
end

-- Smooth dragging: grab the top strip of the menu and it glides after the mouse (Roblox's
-- built-in Draggable snaps every frame and stutters).
do
	local DRAG_STRIP = 30
	local drag = { active = false, offset = nil, target = nil }
	windowFrame.Draggable = false

	local function isPress(input)
		return input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch
	end

	library:connection(userInputService.InputBegan, function(input)
		if not (isPress(input) and windowFrame.Visible) then
			return
		end
		local point = Vector2.new(input.Position.X, input.Position.Y)
		local position, size = windowFrame.AbsolutePosition, windowFrame.AbsoluteSize
		if point.X >= position.X and point.X <= position.X + size.X and point.Y >= position.Y and point.Y <= position.Y + DRAG_STRIP then
			drag.active = true
			drag.offset = point - position
			drag.target = position
			-- Open dropdown / keybind popups don't follow the menu, so close them.
			local open = library.current_element_open
			if open and open.set_visible then
				pcall(open.set_visible, false)
				open.open = false
				library.current_element_open = nil
			end
		end
	end)

	library:connection(userInputService.InputEnded, function(input)
		if isPress(input) then
			drag.active = false
		end
	end)

	library:connection(userInputService.InputChanged, function(input)
		if drag.active and (input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch) then
			drag.target = Vector2.new(input.Position.X, input.Position.Y) - drag.offset
		end
	end)

	library:connection(runService.RenderStepped, function(deltaTime)
		if not drag.target then
			return
		end
		local current = windowFrame.AbsolutePosition
		local nextPosition = current:Lerp(drag.target, 1 - math.exp(-deltaTime * 24))
		if (nextPosition - drag.target).Magnitude < 1.5 then
			nextPosition = drag.target
			drag.target = nil
		end
		-- Position is relative to the menu's gui and its anchor point, in the gui's own units:
		-- on phones the gui is shrunk by a UIScale, so screen pixels are divided back by it.
		-- (Writing raw pixels there meant the menu never reached its target and kept sliding
		-- and shaking on its own.)
		local origin = library.gui.AbsolutePosition
		local guiScale = library.gui:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
		local scale = guiScale and math.max(guiScale.Scale, 0.05) or 1
		local anchor = windowFrame.AnchorPoint * windowFrame.AbsoluteSize
		windowFrame.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(
			math.floor((nextPosition.X - origin.X + anchor.X) / scale + 0.5),
			math.floor((nextPosition.Y - origin.Y + anchor.Y) / scale + 0.5)
		)
	end)
end

-- Keep the menu hidden until the intro finishes.
window.set_menu_visibility(false)

if Hooks.isMobile then
	-- Mobile / tablet: scale UI, resize with viewport, floating menu button, quick toggles.
	local function viewportSize()
		local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
		return cam and cam.ViewportSize or Vector2.new(800, 600)
	end

	local function computeScale()
		local viewport = viewportSize()
		return math.clamp(math.min(viewport.X / 640, viewport.Y / 420), 0.52, 1)
	end

	local uiScale = Instance.new("UIScale")
	uiScale.Scale = computeScale()
	uiScale.Parent = library.gui

	-- Only re-lays out (and re-centers) the menu when the screen really changed size: phones
	-- report tiny viewport changes (bars sliding in and out), which kept snapping it around.
	local lastLayoutSize = nil
	local function layoutMenu()
		local viewport = viewportSize()
		if lastLayoutSize and (viewport - lastLayoutSize).Magnitude < 24 then
			return
		end
		lastLayoutSize = viewport
		local scale = computeScale()
		uiScale.Scale = scale
		local w = math.floor(math.min(560, viewport.X / scale - 16))
		local h = math.floor(math.min(720, viewport.Y / scale - 16))
		windowFrame.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(math.max(280, w), math.max(360, h))
		windowFrame.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		windowFrame.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	end
	layoutMenu()

	local function bindViewport()
		local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
		if cam then
			library:connection(cam:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"), layoutMenu)
		end
	end
	bindViewport()
	library:connection(workspace:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CurrentCamera"), function()
		task.defer(function()
			bindViewport()
			layoutMenu()
		end)
	end)

	local toggleGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
	toggleGui.Name = ""
	toggleGui.ResetOnSpawn = false
	toggleGui.IgnoreGuiInset = true
	toggleGui.DisplayOrder = 100
	toggleGui:SetAttribute("AquaLabs", true)
	toggleGui.Parent = coreGui

	local toggleButton = Instance.new("TextButton")
	toggleButton.Name = ""
	toggleButton.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(54, 54)
	toggleButton.Position = UDim2.new(0, 14, 1, -150)
	toggleButton.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(22, 22, 22)
	toggleButton.AutoButtonColor = false
	toggleButton.Text = "A"
	toggleButton.TextSize = 22
	toggleButton.FontFace = library.font
	toggleButton.TextColor3 = getAccent()
	toggleButton.Parent = toggleGui
	Instance.new("UICorner", toggleButton).CornerRadius = UDim.new(1, 0)
	local toggleStroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	toggleStroke.Color = getAccent()
	toggleStroke.Thickness = 2
	toggleStroke.Parent = toggleButton

	-- Quick bar for features that need a key on PC. The holder carries the bar plus its drag grip
	-- and resize handle (the bar itself lays its buttons out in rows, so the handles sit outside it).
	local quickHolder = Instance.new("Frame")
	quickHolder.Name = ""
	quickHolder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	quickHolder.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 1)
	quickHolder.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, -10)
	quickHolder.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(340, 46)
	quickHolder.Parent = toggleGui
	local quickScale = Instance.new("UIScale")
	quickScale.Parent = quickHolder

	local quickFrame = Instance.new("Frame")
	quickFrame.Name = ""
	quickFrame.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(18, 18, 22)
	quickFrame.BackgroundTransparency = 0.12
	quickFrame.BorderSizePixel = 0
	-- Wraps into rows; you pick which features get a button in Settings > Mobile.
	quickFrame.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(340, 0)
	quickFrame.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
	quickFrame.Active = true
	quickFrame.Parent = quickHolder
	-- The holder takes the bar's height (unscaled), so the handles sit on its corners.
	local function fitHolder()
		local height = quickFrame.AbsoluteSize.Y / math.max(quickScale.Scale, 0.01)
		quickHolder.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(340, math.max(math.floor(height + 0.5), 20))
	end
	quickFrame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(fitHolder)
	Instance.new("UICorner", quickFrame).CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 10)
	local qStroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	qStroke.Color = Color3.fromRGB(55, 55, 75)
	qStroke.Parent = quickFrame
	local qPadding = Instance.new("UIPadding")
	qPadding.PaddingTop, qPadding.PaddingBottom = UDim.new(0, 6), UDim.new(0, 6)
	qPadding.PaddingLeft, qPadding.PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, 6), UDim.new(0, 6)
	qPadding.Parent = quickFrame
	local qLayout = Instance.new("UIListLayout")
	qLayout.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal
	qLayout.HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Center
	qLayout.VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Center
	qLayout.Wraps = true
	qLayout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 6)
	qLayout.Parent = quickFrame

	-- Drag the grip to move the bar, drag the corner handle to resize it. Where you put it is
	-- saved; double-tap the grip to send it back above the hotbar at normal size.
	local BAR_FILE = "Aqua Lab/mobile_bar.json"
	local barState = { custom = false, x = 0, y = 0, scale = 1 }
	pcall(function()
		if isfile(BAR_FILE) then
			local saved = game:GetService("HttpService"):JSONDecode(readfile(BAR_FILE))
			if type(saved) == "table" then
				barState.custom = saved.custom == true
				barState.x, barState.y = tonumber(saved.x) or 0, tonumber(saved.y) or 0
				barState.scale = math.clamp(tonumber(saved.scale) or 1, 0.6, 1.8)
			end
		end
	end)
	local function saveBar()
		pcall(writefile, BAR_FILE, game:GetService("HttpService"):JSONEncode(barState))
	end
	local function applyBar()
		quickScale.Scale = barState.scale
		if barState.custom then
			-- The position is the bar's bottom-middle. Clamped with the bar's real size so all of it
			-- (and both handles) stays on screen; clamping only that point used to park it mostly
			-- off the top-left corner with the drag handle unreachable.
			local viewport = workspace.CurrentCamera.ViewportSize
			quickHolder.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(barState.x, barState.y)
			-- Measure where the bar and both handles really landed (scaling makes predicting it
			-- unreliable) and shift it back by however much sticks out past any edge.
			local margin = 6
			local left, top = math.huge, math.huge
			local right, bottom = NEG_ONE * math.huge, NEG_ONE * math.huge
			for _, child in ipairs(quickHolder:GetChildren()) do
				if child:IsA("GuiObject") then
					local position, size = child.AbsolutePosition, child.AbsoluteSize
					left, top = math.min(left, position.X), math.min(top, position.Y)
					right, bottom = math.max(right, position.X + size.X), math.max(bottom, position.Y + size.Y)
				end
			end
			if left < math.huge then
				local shiftX, shiftY = 0, 0
				if right - left > viewport.X then
					shiftX = viewport.X / 2 + (left + right) / 2 * NEG_ONE
				elseif left < margin then
					shiftX = margin + left * NEG_ONE
				elseif right > viewport.X + NEG_ONE * margin then
					shiftX = viewport.X + NEG_ONE * margin + right * NEG_ONE
				end
				if top < margin then
					shiftY = margin + top * NEG_ONE
				elseif bottom > viewport.Y + NEG_ONE * margin then
					shiftY = viewport.Y + NEG_ONE * margin + bottom * NEG_ONE
				end
				if shiftX ~= 0 or shiftY ~= 0 then
					barState.x, barState.y = barState.x + shiftX, barState.y + shiftY
					quickHolder.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(barState.x, barState.y)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	applyBar()
	-- Again once the bar has its real size, and whenever the screen size changes.
	task.defer(applyBar)
	quickHolder:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(applyBar)
	workspace.CurrentCamera:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(applyBar)

	local function handle(text, position, anchor)
		local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
		button.Name = ""
		button.AnchorPoint = anchor
		button.Position = position
		button.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(26, 26)
		button.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(32, 32, 40)
		button.AutoButtonColor = false
		button.Text = text
		button.TextSize = 16
		button.FontFace = library.font
